records.agency: Parks Canada (Banff National Park)

extra.access_text: Banff NP. Tower removed 1985; the Aylmer Lookout trail still ends at the old site.
extra.structure_note: 40 ft wood tower c.1948; removed 1985 (Potter, via Ron Kemnow)

records.name: Black Rock Lookout
records.agency: Alberta Land and Forest Service (per NHLR)

extra.access_text: Remote alpine ground house west of Calgary; hike or 3-day packhorse trip historically; closed 1950. Reshingled 1995 by Friends of the Eastern Slopes (NHLR).
extra.coord_conflict: Alberta Culture blog (albertashistoricplaces.com, comment, citing ESRD) gives 51 20 30 N 115 11 34 W = 51.3417, -115.1928, about 1.9 km west of the NHLR position
extra.built_note: 1928 per Ron Kemnow (citing Mike Potter) and Mountain Legacy; NHLR says late 1920s; closed 1950 after a trail section collapsed

records.name: Cameron Lookout
records.agency: Alberta Land and Forest Service (per NHLR)

extra.access_text: Highest lookout in Canada when built (about 2,500 m); abandoned 1953, replaced by Raspberry Ridge and Hailstone Butte. Hikeable from Kananaskis (Mount Burke).
extra.built_note: 1929 per Potter/Alberta Culture; a 1937 Calgary Herald quote says the cabin was built 1930; closed 1953

records.name: Castle Mountain Lookout
records.agency: Parks Canada (Banff National Park)

extra.access_text: Banff NP. Only the foundation remains; popular hike from the Bow Valley Parkway (Castle Lookout trail).
extra.coord_note: position is the author's own placement in a Weebly map widget (precision unknown)
extra.built_note: cabin constructed c.1942 (Potter, via Ron Kemnow)

records.name: Chief Mountain Highway Lookout
records.agency: Parks Canada (Waterton Lakes National Park)

extra.access_text: Waterton Lakes NP. 40 ft steel tower north of Chief Mountain Highway, in service about 1958-1973; tower removed in the 1980s; the old forest road up is unmaintained.
extra.built_note: foundations poured autumn 1958; tower reported built by Jan 1959 (Lethbridge Herald)

records.name: Medicine Lodge Lookout
records.agency: Alberta Parks

extra.access_text: Public park site. The original 100 ft steel tower with round crow's nest (1967) was dismantled 1993 and re-established as a 20 ft memorial tower for forest officer Tom Trott; his forestry museum opened here 1997.

extra.access_text: Jasper NP. Popular hike to the former lookout site on the Palisade fire road (Parks Canada says the top of the Palisades was once a lookout site).

records.name: Signal Mountain Lookout
records.agency: Parks Canada (Jasper National Park)

extra.position_note: The survey's position is not used: it is a gazetteer's position of the hill, not the tower's.
extra.access_text: Jasper NP. Decommissioned by 1978 (all Jasper towers). The Signal Mountain fire road / trail leads to the lookout site; whether any structure remains is not stated by these sources.
extra.coord_note: position is the summit of Signal Mountain from the Canadian Rockies peak database, not a surveyed lookout point
extra.built_note: JYHS: constructed 1939; Edmonton Journal 3 Aug 1939 says a lookout was stationed in the warden cabin near the summit; peak database says first mountain-parks lookout was 1941

records.name: Baldy Fire Tower (Riding Mountain National Park)
records.agency: Parks Canada

extra.access_text: Riding Mountain NP towers were phased out in the 1970s; five were still standing in 2018 (a hobbyist visit). Public access not stated.
extra.note: RMNP "Baldy" is a different site from Duck Mountain's Baldy Mountain; no coordinates found; about ten towers were built in the park in 1938-39 (this source)

records.name: Baldy Mountain Fire Tower (Duck Mountain)
records.agency: Manitoba Conservation / Parks

extra.access_text: Public: a 12 m tower on the summit (highest point in Manitoba, 831 m) is kept as a viewing tower with interpretive signs; short paved trail from the parking area on PR 366.
extra.coord_note: author's own Weebly map placement (precision unknown)
notes: a pole lookout tower was built here in 1915 at a cost of $40 (Report of the Director of Forestry, via Ron Kemnow); the present structure is later
a first ranger's cabin and stables are on the summit trail
